title: Why US power transmission needs reinventing
gist: Wood Mackenzie argues the US grid faces a defining contradiction: electricity demand is growing at a pace unseen since the turn of the millennium (data centres alone hitting 20% of total US demand by the end of the 2030s) while high-voltage line completions in the 2020s run at less than half the 2010s rate. The bottleneck is bureaucratic, not technical - cost allocation, permitting and interregional coordination - leaving congestion costs above US$10 billion per year, and FERC Orders 1920/2023, a US$100+ billion ISO/RTO pipeline and DOE's US$1.9 billion SPARK grid-enhancing technology programme only partially close the gap.

insights.claim: US electricity demand is growing at a pace unseen since the turn of the millennium while high-voltage transmission completions in the 2020s are running at half the rate of the 2010s, per Wood Mackenzie.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: A widening physical gap between load growth and wires capacity is structurally bullish for transmission EPC, cable/transformer and grid-equipment suppliers, and for congestion-driven locational power price spreads.
insights.quote: while electricity demand is growing at a pace unseen since the turn of the millennium, high-voltage completions in the 2020s are running at half the rate of the 2010s

insights.claim: Data centres alone will account for 20% of total US electricity demand by the end of the 2030s, with other large loads, electric vehicles and broader electrification adding further pressure, according to Wood Mackenzie.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: A quantified 20% load-share anchor for sizing the data-centre power trade - watch IPPs, gas turbine and nuclear/PPA suppliers with interconnected capacity, since sited-and-energised megawatts become the scarce asset.
insights.quote: By the end of the 2030s, data centres alone will account for 20% of total US electricity demand, with other large loads, electric vehicles and broader electrification adding further pressure.
insights.locator: A defining contradiction: unprecedented demand growth

insights.claim: The average length of high-voltage lines (230 kilovolts and above) completed during the 2020s is less than half the average completed each year in the 2010s, after more than a decade of systematic underbuilding of the US transmission network.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: The 230 kV+ build rate is the single cleanest KPI to track for a transmission upcycle inflection; until it doubles, interconnection scarcity persists regardless of announced pipelines.
insights.quote: the average length of high-voltage transmission lines (i.e., lines operating at 230 kilovolts and above) completed during the 2020s is less than half the average completed each year in the 2010s
insights.locator: Having been systematically underbuilt for over a decade

insights.claim: After more than two decades of more-or-less stagnant demand, US power grids are set to experience almost unprecedented structural growth over the coming decades - a regime change from flat load, not a cyclical uptick.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: Utility and IPP models built on ~0% load growth understate rate base and volume growth; re-rating risk sits with regulated utilities able to grow capex.
insights.quote: After more than two decades of more-or-less stagnant demand, US power grids are set to experience almost unprecedented structural growth over the coming decades.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie attributes the US transmission shortfall mainly to bureaucratic rather than technical causes - cost allocation disputes, fragmented permitting, reactive planning, misaligned utility incentives and weak interregional coordination.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: If the binding constraint is process rather than technology or capital, then policy/regulatory catalysts - not hardware breakthroughs - are the events that reprice transmission-levered equities.
insights.quote: The reasons for the ongoing lack of transmission buildout are mainly bureaucratic rather than technical.
insights.locator: Barriers to buildout are driving up costs

insights.claim: US projects take an average of three years to secure an interconnection agreement, renewable curtailment is rising and congestion costs now exceed US$10 billion per year.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: A US$10bn+ annual congestion pool is the revenue base for FTR/congestion-hedging strategies and for merchant storage sited at constrained nodes; three-year interconnection waits directly haircut renewable developer IRRs.
insights.quote: With projects taking an average of three years to secure an interconnection agreement, renewable curtailment is rising and congestion costs now exceed US$10 billion per year.
insights.locator: The failure to build enough transmission capacity

insights.claim: Transmission shortfalls do not stay local: the failure to build enough capacity produces congestion delays and cascading costs across the entire power value chain, from developers and utilities to large-load consumers, banks and other capital providers.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: Frames grid risk as a credit and financing issue, not just an engineering one - lenders to renewable and large-load projects should price interconnection timing risk explicitly.
insights.quote: The failure to build enough transmission capacity results in congestion delays and cascading costs across the value chain.
insights.locator: The failure to build enough transmission capacity

themes.theme: Reform and capital pipeline vs execution risk

insights.claim: FERC Orders 1920 and 2023 represent significant attempts to reform US power transmission, but FERC must simultaneously incentivise investment and keep customer rates reasonable - a tension Wood Mackenzie flags as unresolved.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: Watch FERC rate-of-return and cost-allocation rulings as the swing factor on whether announced transmission capex actually converts into earned returns for utilities.
insights.quote: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), which sets the rules for the US power sector, is faced with the difficult task of incentivising investments while ensuring reasonable rates for customers.
insights.locator: Despite federal reforms and transmission provider commitments

insights.claim: ISOs and RTOs have announced a US$100+ billion transmission development pipeline, but with many core issues still unaddressed Wood Mackenzie judges execution risk to remain high.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: Do not underwrite the headline US$100bn pipeline at face value - discount for slippage; the gap between announced and energised projects is where transmission-equipment order books disappoint.
insights.quote: The US$100+ billion pipeline for transmission development across plans announced by Independent System Operators (ISOs) and Regional Transmission Organisations (RTOs) is also positive, demonstrating a real commitment to build. However, with many of the core issues still unaddressed, execution risk remains high.
insights.locator: The US$100+ billion pipeline for transmission

themes.theme: GETs as a bridge, not a substitute

insights.claim: In March 2026 the US Department of Energy announced a US$1.9 billion programme, SPARK (Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades), prioritising grid-enhancing technologies.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: A dated, sized federal funding stream for reconductoring and GETs - a near-term revenue catalyst for advanced conductor and sensor vendors ahead of any new-line buildout.
insights.quote: In March 2026, the US Department of Energy announced its US$1.9 billion Speed to Power through Accelerated Reconductoring and other Key Advanced Transmission Technology Upgrades programme (‘SPARK’).

insights.claim: The specific grid-enhancing technologies prioritised by SPARK are dynamic line rating (DLR), topology optimisation, advanced power flow control (APFC) and static line uprating.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: A named shortlist of funded technologies - use it to screen private and listed suppliers in DLR sensors, power-flow control hardware and reconductoring for federal-dollar exposure.
insights.quote: SPARK prioritises grid-enhancing technologies (GETs) including dynamic line rating (DLR), topology optimisation, advanced power flow control (APFC) and static line uprating.

insights.claim: Grid-enhancing technologies only optimise the existing grid as a bridge solution and complement rather than replace new transmission, so they buy time without closing the US transmission gap.
insights.speaker: Siddhant Warrier
insights.so_what: Rejects the bull case that software and reconductoring make new lines unnecessary - the structural scarcity of interconnection capacity persists, keeping constrained-node power and capacity prices elevated.
insights.quote: These technologies provide a bridge solution to optimise the existing grid; however, they complement new transmission rather than replace it.
insights.locator: These technologies provide a bridge solution
